questions.q: A quadcopter, PX4 1.17: the firmware default of `RTL_RETURN_ALT` is 60 m, `rc.mc_defaults` sets 30 m. The operator wrote 45, then set it back to 30. New firmware comes out in which the airframe sets 50 m. What return altitude will there be after the update?
options: 30 m: the operator wrote the value and it was saved
45 m: the first write stayed in storage
50 m: the value 30 never reached storage
60 m: after the update the firmware default applies
questions.explain: `param_export_internal()` does not write values equal to the startup default. 30 matched the airframe default, so it is not in the BSON, and after the update the parameter gets the new airframe default, 50 m. 60 m would only apply without an airframe.

questions.q: You typed `param import /fs/microsd/backup.bson`, and the values in `param show` are right. After a reboot the old ones are back. Why?
options: Import marks the values as saved and does not trigger an autosave; you need `param save`
`param import` reads only the `CAL_*` parameters and skips the rest
A file on the SD card can only be read with `param load`
Autosave is disabled while USB is connected to the board
questions.explain: In `param_import_callback()` the values are written with the mark_saved flag, and `param_autosave()` is called only for unsaved changes. The main storage stays as it was until you type `param save` or change any other parameter.

questions.q: PX4 1.17: which reset keeps the accelerometer calibration (`CAL_ACC*`) and the radio (`RC*`)?
options: The console `param reset_all` with no arguments
QGC: Reset all to firmware's defaults
QGC: Reset to vehicle's configuration defaults
`param load` with no arguments
questions.explain: That QGC item writes `SYS_AUTOCONFIG`, and at boot `rcS` runs `param reset_all SYS_AUTOSTART SYS_PARAM_VER RC* CAL_* COM_FLTMODE* LND_FLIGHT* TC_* COM_FLIGHT*`. The console reset with no arguments erases everything, firmware's defaults keeps only the flight time and `COM_FLIGHT_UUID`. In 1.18.0 `RC*` and `COM_FLTMODE*` were dropped from this list.

questions.q: `listener sensor_gps` prints coordinates, while QGC reports GPS lost. What do you type next?
options: `listener sensor_gps -i 1` to see the second instance
`listener sensor_gps -n 5` to wait for new messages
`param show GPS*` to check the port settings
`uorb status` to see the topic's queue size
questions.explain: Without `-n`, listener prints the last published message even if it is old. With `-n 5` it waits for new ones and after 2 s prints "Waited for 2.0 seconds without a message. Giving up.": then the driver is silent, and next come `gps status` and `dmesg`.

questions.q: In SITL (`pxh>`) the `top` command answers `command not found`. How do you see the CPU load?
options: `top once`: SITL supports only a one-shot output
`ps`: the NuttX task list with CPU share
`dmesg`: it has a CPU usage line
`listener cpuload` and `work_queue status`
questions.explain: `boards/px4/sitl/default.px4board` has no `CONFIG_SYSTEMCMDS_TOP`, `DMESG` or `REBOOT`, and `ps` is an nsh built-in that pxh does not have. The `cpuload` topic is published by `load_mon`, and `work_queue status` shows the rates of the queue items.

questions.q: Parameters were saved 0.5 s ago. You change one more. When does the autosave fire?
options: After 0.3 s
After 1.5 s
After 2.0 s
After 2.3 s
questions.explain: `ParamAutosave::request()`: a delay of 0.3 s, but no more than one save per 2 s, so `max(0.3, 2 − 0.5)` = 1.5 s.

questions.q: In `config.txt` you need a value that applies on every vehicle, but the operator can change it in QGC and the change sticks. Which command?
options: `param set <name> <value>`
`param set <name> <value> fail`
`param set-default <name> <value>`
`param touch <name>` and the value in `extras.txt`
questions.explain: `param set-default` changes the startup default, a lower layer; the value saved by the operator sits above it and wins. `param set` in `config.txt` runs on every boot and overrides what QGC wrote.

questions.q: The first vehicle's `.params`, including `CAL_ACC*`, was loaded onto a second vehicle with the same board model. What happens to the accelerometer calibration check?
options: It fails: `CAL_ACC0_ID` holds the other sensor's serial number
QGC refuses to load the file: the board's `PX4GUID` does not match
`CAL_*` parameters are not in `.params`, so the calibration does not change
It passes: the IDs match, but the offsets are someone else's
questions.explain: A device ID is the bus type, bus number, address and chip type, with no serial number. On a board of the same model it matches, `FindCurrentCalibrationIndex()` finds the entry, the check passes, and the offsets and scales come from another unit. QGC checks only the System Id.

questions.q: `MAV_1_RATE` is not in the QGC list. `param find MAV_1_RATE` answers "Found param … at index …", `param show MAV_1_RATE` prints nothing. What do you do?
options: Rebuild the firmware via `boardconfig` with the mavlink module
Write `MAV_1_CONFIG` ≠ 0 and reboot the board
Run `param reset MAV_1_RATE` and refresh the list
Nothing: the parameter is for planes and hidden on a multicopter
questions.explain: The parameter is in the build but not used: the MAVLink instance start command reads it, and `rc.serial` runs that only when a port is assigned. QGC gets only the used parameters from the firmware.

questions.q: `commander check` in the MAVLink Console answered `Preflight check: FAILED` and nothing else. How do you find the reason without the QGC panel?
options: `commander arm -f`: the reason appears in the arming reply
`commander status`: the reason is in the navigation mode line
`dmesg`: the `Preflight Fail: …` lines from commander
`param show -c`: the reason is marked with an asterisk
questions.explain: The check messages are printed by the commander task, and the MAVLink shell shows only the output of the command run in it. `dmesg` reads the console buffer. The `FAILED` line itself is the result of the previous evaluation: the command starts a new one, its reasons arrive a second later, and a repeated `commander check` shows the fresh result. `commander arm -f` shows no reasons: it bypasses the checks and starts the motors.
